provenance.original: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s VID and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 222 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 990 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 230 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 12 minutes (0.2 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 21,418.5 hours, or 64,256 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.

provenance.original: TSA uses historical data from the LEO Flying Armed Application which vets and stores all National Law Enforcement Telecommunications System messages (known as flying while armed messages) submitted by state, local, and tribal LEOs.  Based on this data, TSA estimates an average annual number of 83,749 responses to this collection.  Each response consists of filling out a short form at the screening checkpoint.  TSA estimates that the time burden for this activity is 4 minute (0.0667 hours).  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be 5,583 hours per year (16,750 hours over the 3-year period).  Respondents to this collection are state, local, tribal, and territorial LEOs travelling on official business, therefore TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage rate of $64.48 to estimate the hour burden cost.  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be $359,990.  Table 1 summarizes these calculations.

provenance.original: Applicants who enroll or renew in a TSA Agent State consist of three types of respondents: new enrollments, online renewals, and in-person renewals.  TSA estimates 48 percent of applicants will be new enrollments, and 52 percent will be renewals.  All new enrollments must be done in person, with the option of conducting an online pre-enrollment, while renewals may be done online.  TSA estimates 60 percent of the renewals will be done online, while the remaining 40 percent will be done in person.  Table 4 shows the calculations.

provenance.original: TSA will be implementing the ability for online renewals or re-enrollment capability for applicants.  Active HME holders will be able to renew online before their STA expires; HME holders who have a recently expired STA will be able to re-enroll online.  Approximately 52 percent of active HME holders renew their HME when it expires every 5 years.  Online HME renewals will reduce the applicant’s cost and hour burden by avoiding visiting a TSA enrollment center for the renewal of an STA.  TSA estimates the online renewal time burden to be 10 minutes (0.17 hours), and calculates the total time burden by multiplying the number of online renewals as shown in column (N) of Table 5(c).  Also, due to the reduced cost of the online enrollment transaction, the renewal fee for an HME STA will decrease.  TSA estimates 60 percent of renewals through TSA Agent States will be done online.  The calculations are summarized in Table 5(c).
